entries.clue: Separate clue for trifle? (6,3)

blocks.note: the six letters of trifle in a different order
out, as in out of order, is a standard instruction to rearrange the letters before it

annotation.surface: Someone asking for a crossword clue for the pudding trifle.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer is not built from 'trifle', it is the instruction that would clue it, with OUT naming what was done to FILTER's letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To filter out is to separate unwanted matter from the rest.

entries.clue: Top quality match enveloped by lots of passion (4-4)

indicators.note: the match is wrapped inside the other letters
most of the word, not all of it: the last letter goes

blocks.note: FIRE, a word for passion, without its last letter
a vesta is an old word for a short match

annotation.surface: A thrilling contest full of passion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting contest, but it is the kind you strike: a vesta is a short wax match, a word now met mostly in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Five-star, as in hotel ratings, means of the highest quality.

entries.clue: From time to time, look to fate (3)

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter

blocks.note: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of LOOKTO

annotation.surface: Advice to trust in destiny every so often.
annotation.walkthrough: 'to' does double duty in the surface but the fodder runs across the gap: L-O-o-K-T-o.
annotation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fate in life.

entries.clue: Unusual case passed on to up the intensity (8)

indicators.note: the letters of case appear in an unusual order

blocks.note: CASE rearranged
the late X is the X who has died

annotation.surface: An odd legal case handed up the chain to raise the stakes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passed on' looks like handing something over; here it is the euphemism for dead, giving LATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a row or a war that escalates climbs step by step, like the escalator the word comes from.

entries.clue: Go round the bend endlessly in French department (4)

indicators.note: without its ends, so both first and last letters go

blocks.note: CORNER (to go round a bend) without its C and R

annotation.surface: Going mad without end somewhere in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go round the bend' wants to mean go mad; read literally it is CORNER. Orne is a department of Normandy.
annotation.definitionFit: Orne is one of France's administrative departments.

entries.clue: Desk, left out with salt during religious teaching in church (10)

indicators.note: a thing left out is omitted, so the L that stands for left is omitted from the desk
the salt goes inside the religious teaching

blocks.note: TABLE without its L
RE, religious education, the school subject
NaCl, the chemical formula for common salt

annotation.surface: A pew-side lectern and a salt cellar at a scripture lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salt' usually tempts a solver towards a sailor (AB or TAR); here it is chemistry. RE, religious education, is the British school subject.
annotation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a place of worship, especially a nonconformist or Mormon church.

entries.clue: Running about on leave in part of the Western US (6)

indicators.note: ON goes about, around, the rest

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on
re = on, concerning
to leave is to go

annotation.surface: Jogging around while on holiday out West.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On leave' reads as holiday, but the two words split apart and each gives its own chunk, which is why the same little word appears twice in different roles.
annotation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state on the Pacific coast of the United States.

entries.clue: Some cards for football team (6)

blocks.note: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
the short name of Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club

annotation.surface: Yellow and red cards being shown to a football team.
annotation.walkthrough: Football sets up booking cards; the cards are a suit, and Hearts is a Scottish club.
annotation.definitionFit: Hearts is both a card suit and the usual name of Heart of Midlothian FC.

entries.clue: Exposed appliance for removing water from locks in Scottish town (7)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, so first and last letters go

blocks.clueFragment: Exposed appliance for removing water from locks
blocks.note: HAIRDRIER without its H and R

annotation.surface: A hairdryer with bare wires found in a Scottish town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests canals, but they are hair; the appliance is a HAIRDRIER. Airdrie is a town east of Glasgow.
annotation.definitionFit: Airdrie is a town in North Lanarkshire, Scotland.

entries.clue: Polish ruse to muddle Trump, perhaps (10)

indicators.note: the letters are to be muddled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A cunning trick from Poland designed to confuse the US president.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish' leads with its capital to Poland; it is only letters. The definition is a jibe at Donald Trump's perceived fondness for Russia, hence 'perhaps'.
annotation.definitionFit: A Russophile admires Russia, which critics have said of Trump.

entries.clue: One entering vacant, dilapidated palace (7)

indicators.note: the I goes into the other word
falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
taken as it stands, then rearranged with the I

annotation.surface: A squatter moving into an empty, run-down palace.
annotation.walkthrough: The run-down empty palace turns out to be the grandest one of all: the Vatican.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Pope's official residence in Rome is a palace, and the most famous one there is.

entries.clue: Current supplier from Spain quit over stealing stereo, essentially (9)

indicators.note: RESIGN takes the letters into itself
the essence, the middle, of the word
turned over, so read backwards

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
to resign is to quit a job
the middle two letters of stEREo

annotation.surface: A Spanish shop worker walking out after pinching a hi-fi.
annotation.walkthrough: The container is built first and only then turned round, so assemble before reversing. 'Current' is electric current, and Energizer is a battery brand.
annotation.definitionFit: An energiser, like a battery, supplies electric current.

entries.clue: Humble Earl limps around (6)

indicators.note: the letters are moved around

blocks.note: E = earl, a standard abbreviation
anagram fodder with the E

annotation.surface: A modest aristocrat hobbling about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Humble Earl' reads as one phrase, but 'Humble' is the definition and the earl is just E.
annotation.definitionFit: Simple and humble both describe a modest, unpretentious life.

entries.clue: Case of archetypal sucker stopping to pay for "financial security" (4,6)

indicators.note: the casing, the outer letters, of the word
plugging a gap in the other word

blocks.note: to meet a cost is to pay for it
the outer letters of ArchetypaL
a tick is a bloodsucking parasite

annotation.surface: A typical gullible customer holding up payment for a pension scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a dupe, but it is a bloodsucker: the TICK. AL and TICK together fill MEET.
annotation.definitionFit: A meal ticket is a person or thing relied on as a source of income.

entries.clue: Somehow stop dismal singer (10)

indicators.note: arranged in some way or other

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A plea to silence a dreary vocalist.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'dismal singer' as a phrase, but 'dismal' belongs with 'stop' as the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrower term: someone who sings or composes psalms, so a particular kind of singer.

entries.clue: Chicken specialist collects old flightless birds (7)

indicators.note: someone who collects a thing gathers it in, so the restaurant name gathers the O inside it

blocks.note: Nando's, the chain of chicken restaurants
O = old, a standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A poultry restaurant gathering up aged ostriches.
annotation.walkthrough: Nando's is a peri-peri chicken restaurant chain, common in Britain. Nandoo (or nandu) is another name for the rhea.
annotation.definitionFit: Nandoos, or rheas, are large flightless South American birds.

entries.clue: Russian card game that doesn't use clubs is back — back in Russia (9)

indicators.note: leaves out the letter for clubs
something that is back has returned the way it came, so the word runs in the opposite direction
the back, last, letter of the word

blocks.clueFragment: card game that doesn't use clubs
blocks.note: CANASTA without C, clubs
IS reversed
the last letter of RussiA

annotation.surface: A Russian card game played without clubs making a comeback there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Russian card game' wants to be one phrase; 'Russian' is the definition and canasta is from South America. Anastasia was the Tsar's youngest daughter.
annotation.definitionFit: Anastasia is a Russian, most famously Grand Duchess Anastasia Romanov.

entries.clue: Regularly shoot and record stuff as 3-D image (8)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, every second letter

blocks.note: the 2nd and 4th letters of sHoOt
to log is to record
to ram is to stuff or cram

annotation.surface: Filming and saving footage as a three-dimensional picture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoot and record' paints filming; only HO comes from 'shoot', and 'record' and 'stuff' are verbs.
annotation.definitionFit: A hologram is a three-dimensional image made with lasers.

entries.clue: Most of country upset over one's failure to develop (8)

indicators.note: most of a word is nearly all of it, so the country loses just its final letter
turned upside down, which in a down clue reverses it

blocks.note: SENEGAL without its L
one's = one is, I'S

annotation.surface: Much of a nation unhappy at someone's stunted growth.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first part on top of the second. The country is Senegal.
annotation.definitionFit: Agenesis is the failure of an organ or body part to develop.

entries.clue: Hanging around work, walking with a bounce (9)

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so the word for hanging surrounds the word for work

blocks.note: lolling = hanging loosely, like a tongue
OP = opus, a work

annotation.surface: Loafing about at the office, then bouncing off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hanging around work' reads as idling, but 'around' is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move with a clumsy bounding gait.

entries.clue: Something pointed close to some farm animals (7)

indicators.note: the close, last letter, of the word

blocks.note: the last letter of somE
a PIG and a RAM

annotation.surface: A sharp object lying near livestock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' suggests something sharp to touch; the point is in the wit.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist on a stock phrase: epigrams are proverbially pointed, their point being a sharp witty sting rather than a physical tip.

entries.clue: Whole of Ireland absorbing part of the Bible (6)

indicators.note: taking the letters into itself

blocks.note: Éire, the Irish name for Ireland
NT = New Testament

annotation.surface: All of Ireland soaking up scripture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whole of Ireland' reads as one phrase; 'Whole' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the entire cake and the whole cake are the same cake, with nothing missing.

entries.clue: Prayers in bed? (6)

blocks.note: the Catholic sequence of prayers counted on beads
a flower bed, specifically one planted with roses

annotation.surface: Saying one's prayers before sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests bedtime, but it is a flower bed; the question mark flags the second, rarer sense of rosary.
annotation.definitionFit: A rosary is a sequence of prayers, and also a bed of roses.

entries.clue: Lead piping over new houses (6)

indicators.note: the words house the answer inside them

blocks.note: pipinG OVER New

annotation.surface: Old lead water pipes installed in new homes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead piping' is the plumbing picture; 'Lead' is the verb to rule and the pipes are just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a party that governs a country leads it.

entries.clue: Attempts to shoot fish for select party (4,5)

blocks.note: a take is one filmed attempt at a scene
an ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A film crew's attempts to film fish for an exclusive gathering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' could mean fire at the fish; it is filming, and 'select party' is a verb and object, not an exclusive do.
annotation.definitionFit: To take sides is to choose which party to support.

entries.clue: South American iron is reliable (4)

blocks.note: SA = South America(n)
Fe, the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: A tribute to the dependability of Latin American steelwork.
annotation.walkthrough: Two abbreviations: the continent and the element.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a safe bet or a safe driver is one you can rely on.

entries.clue: By the way, a very big rugby player is boring (7)

indicators.note: the player bores into the other letters

blocks.note: as written
OS = outsize, a clothing size
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

annotation.surface: An aside that a huge rugby forward is dull company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it is the drilling kind: PROP bores into A…OS. 'Very big rugby player' wants to be one person; OS and PROP are separate.
annotation.definitionFit: Apropos, used to change the subject, means by the way.

entries.clue: Discharge Manx cat? (3)

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a familiar word for a cat, minus its tail, the final letter

annotation.surface: Letting go of a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
annotation.walkthrough: The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, is born without a tail, so it is an instruction to dock the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense of discharge, the medical one: matter that seeps from an infected wound.

entries.clue: Goes to bed in garret I reserved (7)

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

blocks.note: garRET I REServed

annotation.surface: Someone turning in for the night in an attic room they had booked.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across all three words, straddling the lone I.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal, slightly old-fashioned sense: one retires for the night, withdrawing to one's bedroom.

entries.clue: Scratching head, remaining prophet provides bottles of drink? (9)

indicators.note: the head, first letter, is scratched out

blocks.note: OTHER (remaining, as in the other ones) without its O
Moses, the Old Testament prophet

annotation.surface: A puzzled prophet handing out flasks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' pictures puzzlement; it is an instruction to drop a first letter. The question mark is because thermoses hold drink rather than being bottles of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Thermoses are vacuum flasks for keeping drinks hot or cold.
